1	"""Columnar execution engine.
2	
3	The scanner reads each CSV table in record batches of at most
4	:data:`BATCH_SIZE` rows, materializing only the columns referenced by the
5	SELECT list, the GROUP BY key or the WHERE clause (column pruning).
6	Within a batch the predicate — an AND/OR/parentheses boolean tree of
7	column-op-value comparisons — is evaluated column-at-a-time *before*
8	projection or grouping (predicate pushdown), and aggregates — either a
9	single global row or per-group hash tables keyed by one GROUP BY column
10	or a tuple of several GROUP BY columns — roll forward batch by batch.
11	Besides ``count(*)``, the column aggregates are ``sum``, ``avg``, ``min``
12	and ``max``: sums and average accumulators add every matched row's cell,
13	min/max keep the extreme value seen so far. On an empty filtered input the
14	global ``avg``/``min``/``max`` results are null (and compare false in
15	HAVING) while ``sum`` is 0; empty inputs produce no groups at all.
16	HAVING, when present, is evaluated only after the aggregates have been
17	exactly computed: it drops the global row or individual groups, never
18	individual input rows.
19	
20	ORDER BY, when present, sorts the surviving result rows — after WHERE,
21	aggregation and HAVING — by one or more SELECT result columns, each with
22	its own ASC (default) or DESC direction. Finite-decimal values compare by
23	exact numeric value (``1`` equals ``1.0``); everything else compares by
24	raw text, never coerced to a number. Multi-item keys compare left to
25	right; rows equal on every key keep their incoming order (CSV row order
26	for projections, first-appearance order for groups). LIMIT, when present,
27	truncates the sorted rows last.
28	
29	Every cell read by a numeric comparison is parsed eagerly for every row
30	of a batch, even on rows whose other OR branches already settle the
31	outcome: OR never short-circuits cell validation, so a non-numeric cell
32	anywhere a numeric predicate reaches fails the whole query.
33	
34	All arithmetic and numeric comparison go through :class:`decimal.Decimal`
35	so results are deterministic and free of binary-float artifacts.
36	"""
37	
38	from __future__ import annotations
39	
40	import csv
41	from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation
42	from pathlib import Path
43	from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple
44	
45	from .sql import (
46	    Comparison,
47	    HavingComparison,
48	    HavingExpr,
49	    Query,
50	    SelectItem,
51	    SortItem,
52	    WhereExpr,
53	    parse_sql,
54	)
55	
56	BATCH_SIZE = 1024
57	
58	# Column aggregates over finite decimals, besides count(*).
59	_AGG_KINDS = ("sum", "avg", "min", "max")
60	
61	# Aggregate state and final values are keyed by (kind, column); a state's
62	# value is a running Decimal for sum/avg, the extreme Decimal so far for
63	# min/max (None until a row matches).
64	_AggKey = Tuple[str, str]
65	
66	
67	def _decimal(field: str, column: str) -> Decimal:
68	    try:
69	        value = Decimal(field)
70	    except (InvalidOperation, ValueError):
71	        raise ValueError(
72	            f"column {column!r} contains non-numeric value {field!r}"
73	        )
74	    if not value.is_finite():
75	        raise ValueError(
76	            f"column {column!r} contains non-numeric value {field!r}"
77	        )
78	    return value
79	
80	
81	def _compare(left: Any, op: str, right: Any) -> bool:
82	    if op == "=":
83	        return left == right
84	    if op == "!=":
85	        return left != right
86	    if op == ">":
87	        return left > right
88	    if op == ">=":
89	        return left >= right
90	    if op == "<":
91	        return left < right
92	    return left <= right  # "<="
93	
94	
95	def _column_vector(rows: Sequence[Sequence[str]], idx: int) -> List[str]:
96	    """Extract one column from a row batch; short rows yield empty fields."""
97	    vec: List[str] = []
98	    for row in rows:
99	        vec.append(row[idx] if idx < len(row) else "")
100	    return vec
101	
102	
103	def _comparison_vector(
104	    rows: Sequence[Sequence[str]],
105	    col_index: Dict[str, int],
106	    comp: Comparison,
107	) -> List[bool]:
108	    """Evaluate one comparison over every row of the batch.
109	
110	    The column is parsed for *every* row up front, including rows whose
111	    other OR branches already decide the row: OR does not short-circuit
112	    cell validation.
113	    """
114	    idx = col_index[comp.column]
115	    vec = _column_vector(rows, idx)
116	    result: List[bool] = [False] * len(vec)
117	    if comp.quoted:
118	        target_text = comp.value_text
119	        for i, field in enumerate(vec):
120	            result[i] = _compare(field, comp.op, target_text)
121	    else:
122	        target = Decimal(comp.value_text)
123	        for i, field in enumerate(vec):
124	            result[i] = _compare(_decimal(field, comp.column), comp.op, target)
125	    return result
126	
127	
128	def _combine(op: str, vectors: Sequence[Sequence[bool]]) -> List[bool]:
129	    """Combine per-row boolean vectors with AND or OR."""
130	    if op == "AND":
131	        mask = [True] * len(vectors[0])
132	        for vec in vectors:
133	            for i, value in enumerate(vec):
134	                mask[i] = mask[i] and value
135	        return mask
136	    mask = [False] * len(vectors[0])
137	    for vec in vectors:
138	        for i, value in enumerate(vec):
139	            mask[i] = mask[i] or value
140	    return mask
141	
142	
143	def _eval_node(
144	    node: WhereExpr,
145	    rows: Sequence[Sequence[str]],
146	    col_index: Dict[str, int],
147	) -> List[bool]:
148	    """Vectorized boolean-tree evaluation on raw columns."""
149	    if isinstance(node, Comparison):
150	        return _comparison_vector(rows, col_index, node)
151	    vectors = [_eval_node(operand, rows, col_index) for operand in node.operands]
152	    return _combine(node.op, vectors)
153	
154	
155	def _evaluate_predicate(
156	    rows: List[Sequence[str]],
157	    col_index: Dict[str, int],
158	    where: WhereExpr,
159	) -> List[bool]:
160	    """Vectorized predicate tree; runs on raw columns, ahead of projection."""
161	    return _eval_node(where, rows, col_index)
162	
163	
164	def _eval_having(
165	    node: HavingExpr, count: int, values: Dict[_AggKey, Optional[Decimal]]
166	) -> bool:
167	    """Evaluate a HAVING tree against one fully computed aggregate row.
168	
169	    Left operands are always numeric (an integer row count or an exactly
170	    computed Decimal aggregate); textual aggregate results are never
171	    coerced, and the right operands are the parser-validated finite decimal
172	    literals. A null aggregate — avg/min/max over an empty global input —
173	    makes its comparison false.
174	    """
175	    if isinstance(node, HavingComparison):
176	        if node.kind == "count_star":
177	            left: Decimal = Decimal(count)
178	        else:
179	            value = values[(node.kind, node.column)]
180	            if value is None:
181	                return False
182	            left = value
183	        return _compare(left, node.op, Decimal(node.value_text))
184	    if node.op == "AND":
185	        return all(_eval_having(operand, count, values) for operand in node.operands)
186	    return any(_eval_having(operand, count, values) for operand in node.operands)
187	
188	
189	def _project_value(field: str) -> Any:
190	    """Infer a projected cell: decimal-able text becomes a JSON number."""
191	    try:
192	        value = Decimal(field)
193	    except (InvalidOperation, ValueError):
194	        return field
195	    if not value.is_finite():
196	        return field
197	    if value == value.to_integral_value():
198	        return int(value)
199	    return value
200	
201	
202	def _number(value: Decimal) -> Any:
203	    """Render an aggregate value as int when integral, else keep Decimal."""
204	    if value == value.to_integral_value():
205	        return int(value)
206	    return value
207	
208	
209	def _group_key(field: str) -> Any:
210	    """Normalize a grouping cell.
211	
212	    Finite decimal text groups by exact decimal value (so ``1`` and
213	    ``1.0`` share a group); everything else groups by raw text.
214	    """
215	    try:
216	        value = Decimal(field)
217	    except (InvalidOperation, ValueError):
218	        return field
219	    if not value.is_finite():
220	        return field
221	    return value
222	
223	
224	def _key_output(key: Any) -> Any:
225	    """Render a grouping key for JSON: numeric keys follow projection rules."""
226	    if isinstance(key, Decimal):
227	        return _number(key)
228	    return key
229	
230	
231	def _new_agg_state(agg_items: Sequence[SelectItem]) -> Dict[_AggKey, Optional[Decimal]]:
232	    """Fresh per-row-stream aggregate state.
233	
234	    sum/avg start at a zero running sum; min/max start empty (None) until
235	    the first matched row supplies a value.
236	    """
237	    state: Dict[_AggKey, Optional[Decimal]] = {}
238	    for item in agg_items:
239	        key = (item.kind, item.column)
240	        state[key] = None if item.kind in ("min", "max") else Decimal(0)
241	    return state
242	
243	
244	def _accumulate(
245	    state: Dict[_AggKey, Optional[Decimal]],
246	    agg_items: Sequence[SelectItem],
247	    row: Sequence[str],
248	    col_index: Dict[str, int],
249	) -> None:
250	    """Roll one matched row into the aggregate state."""
251	    for item in agg_items:
252	        idx = col_index[item.column]
253	        field = row[idx] if idx < len(row) else ""
254	        value = _decimal(field, item.column)
255	        key = (item.kind, item.column)
256	        current = state[key]
257	        if item.kind in ("sum", "avg"):
258	            state[key] = current + value
259	        elif item.kind == "min":
260	            if current is None or value < current:
261	                state[key] = value
262	        else:  # "max"
263	            if current is None or value > current:
264	                state[key] = value
265	
266	
267	def _final_values(
268	    agg_items: Sequence[SelectItem],
269	    count: int,
270	    state: Dict[_AggKey, Optional[Decimal]],
271	) -> Dict[_AggKey, Optional[Decimal]]:
272	    """Finalize one aggregate state into output values.
273	
274	    avg divides its exact running sum by the exact row count (Decimal
275	    division, free of binary-float artifacts); min/max stay as recorded.
276	    On an empty input avg/min/max are None (JSON null) while sum is 0.
277	    """
278	    final: Dict[_AggKey, Optional[Decimal]] = {}
279	    for item in agg_items:
280	        key = (item.kind, item.column)
281	        value = state[key]
282	        if item.kind == "avg":
283	            final[key] = None if count == 0 else value / count
284	        else:
285	            final[key] = value
286	    return final
287	
288	
289	def _aggregate_result(
290	    query: Query, count: int, values: Dict[_AggKey, Optional[Decimal]]
291	) -> Dict[str, Any]:
292	    row: List[Any] = []
293	    for item in query.select:
294	        if item.kind == "count_star":
295	            row.append(count)
296	        else:
297	            value = values[(item.kind, item.column)]
298	            row.append(None if value is None else _number(value))
299	    return {
300	        "columns": [item.text for item in query.select],
301	        "rows": [row],
302	        "row_count": 1,
303	    }
304	
305	
306	def _grouped_result(
307	    query: Query,
308	    order: List[Tuple[Any, ...]],
309	    counts: Dict[Tuple[Any, ...], int],
310	    values: Dict[Tuple[Any, ...], Dict[_AggKey, Optional[Decimal]]],
311	) -> Dict[str, Any]:
312	    group_cols = query.group_by
313	    rows: List[List[Any]] = []
314	    for key in order:
315	        row: List[Any] = []
316	        for pos, item in enumerate(query.select):
317	            if pos < len(group_cols):
318	                # The leading SELECT items are the GROUP BY columns, in order.
319	                row.append(_key_output(key[pos]))
320	            elif item.kind == "count_star":
321	                row.append(counts[key])
322	            else:
323	                value = values[key][(item.kind, item.column)]
324	                row.append(None if value is None else _number(value))
325	        rows.append(row)
326	    return {
327	        "columns": [item.text for item in query.select],
328	        "rows": rows,
329	        "row_count": len(rows),
330	    }
331	
332	
333	def _sort_key(value: Any) -> Tuple[int, Any]:
334	    """Order key for one result cell.
335	
336	    Finite decimals (already int/Decimal after projection, key rendering or
337	    aggregation) compare by exact numeric value, so ``1`` and ``1.0`` tie;
338	    everything else compares by raw text and is never coerced to a number.
339	    Numbers order before text so mixed columns stay deterministic.
340	    """
341	    if isinstance(value, (int, Decimal)) and not isinstance(value, bool):
342	        return (0, Decimal(value))
343	    return (1, str(value))
344	
345	
346	def _apply_order_by(
347	    result: Dict[str, Any],
348	    order_by: Tuple[SortItem, ...],
349	    select: Tuple[SelectItem, ...],
350	) -> None:
351	    """Sort result rows in place, one stable pass per item, last item first.
352	
353	    Each sort item was validated against the SELECT list at parse time, so
354	    its column position always resolves. Stability keeps rows that tie on
355	    every key in their incoming order (CSV row order for projections,
356	    first-appearance order for groups).
357	    """
358	    rows = result["rows"]
359	    for item in reversed(order_by):
360	        idx = next(
361	            pos
362	            for pos, si in enumerate(select)
363	            if si.kind == item.kind and si.column == item.column
364	        )
365	        rows.sort(key=lambda row, i=idx: _sort_key(row[i]), reverse=item.descending)
366	
367	
368	def _apply_limit(result: Dict[str, Any], limit: int) -> None:
369	    """Truncate result rows in place; LIMIT 0 keeps columns, empties rows."""
370	    del result["rows"][limit:]
371	    result["row_count"] = len(result["rows"])
372	
373	
374	def _run_batches(
375	    reader: csv.reader,
376	    query: Query,
377	    header: Sequence[str],
378	) -> Dict[str, Any]:
379	    col_index = {name: header.index(name) for name in query.required_columns()}
380	
381	    projected_rows: List[List[Any]] = []
382	    count = 0
383	    select_cols: Tuple[SelectItem, ...] = query.select
384	    agg_items = [item for item in select_cols if item.kind in _AGG_KINDS]
385	    state = _new_agg_state(agg_items)
386	
387	    if query.is_grouped:
388	        # First-appearance order of composite group keys over the
389	        # filtered row stream.
390	        order: List[Tuple[Any, ...]] = []
391	        group_counts: Dict[Tuple[Any, ...], int] = {}
392	        group_states: Dict[Tuple[Any, ...], Dict[_AggKey, Optional[Decimal]]] = {}
393	        group_idxs = [col_index[name] for name in query.group_by]
394	
395	        while True:
396	            batch = [row for _, row in zip(range(BATCH_SIZE), reader)]
397	            if not batch:
398	                break
399	            mask = (
400	                [True] * len(batch)
401	                if query.where is None
402	                else _evaluate_predicate(batch, col_index, query.where)
403	            )
404	            for i, matched in enumerate(mask):
405	                if not matched:
406	                    continue
407	                row = batch[i]
408	                key = tuple(
409	                    _group_key(row[idx] if idx < len(row) else "")
410	                    for idx in group_idxs
411	                )
412	                if key not in group_counts:
413	                    group_counts[key] = 0
414	                    group_states[key] = _new_agg_state(agg_items)
415	                    order.append(key)
416	                group_counts[key] += 1
417	                _accumulate(group_states[key], agg_items, row, col_index)
418	
419	        # Finalize every group exactly before HAVING or output; groups
420	        # always hold at least one row, so their avg/min/max are non-null.
421	        group_values = {
422	            key: _final_values(agg_items, group_counts[key], group_states[key])
423	            for key in order
424	        }
425	        if query.having is not None:
426	            # HAVING runs after every group has been exactly computed and
427	            # only drops whole groups; first-appearance order is preserved.
428	            order = [
429	                key
430	                for key in order
431	                if _eval_having(query.having, group_counts[key], group_values[key])
432	            ]
433	        return _grouped_result(query, order, group_counts, group_values)
434	
435	    while True:
436	        batch = [row for _, row in zip(range(BATCH_SIZE), reader)]
437	        if not batch:
438	            break
439	        mask = (
440	            [True] * len(batch)
441	            if query.where is None
442	            else _evaluate_predicate(batch, col_index, query.where)
443	        )
444	
445	        if query.is_aggregate:
446	            for i, matched in enumerate(mask):
447	                if not matched:
448	                    continue
449	                count += 1
450	                _accumulate(state, agg_items, batch[i], col_index)
451	        else:
452	            indices = [col_index[item.column] for item in select_cols]
453	            for i, matched in enumerate(mask):
454	                if not matched:
455	                    continue
456	                row = batch[i]
457	                projected_rows.append(
458	                    [
459	                        _project_value(row[idx] if idx < len(row) else "")
460	                        for idx in indices
461	                    ]
462	                )
463	
464	    if query.is_aggregate:
465	        values = _final_values(agg_items, count, state)
466	        result = _aggregate_result(query, count, values)
467	        if query.having is not None and not _eval_having(
468	            query.having, count, values
469	        ):
470	            # A global aggregate always computes one row; HAVING failing
471	            # leaves the same columns but no rows.
472	            result["rows"] = []
473	            result["row_count"] = 0
474	        return result
475	    return {
476	        "columns": [item.text for item in select_cols],
477	        "rows": projected_rows,
478	        "row_count": len(projected_rows),
479	    }
480	
481	
482	def _dumps(obj: Any) -> str:
483	    """Deterministic JSON encoder; Decimal values render as decimal numbers."""
484	
485	    def encode(value: Any) -> str:
486	        if value is None:
487	            return "null"
488	        if value is True:
489	            return "true"
490	        if isinstance(value, bool):
491	            return "false"
492	        if isinstance(value, Decimal):
493	            return format(value, "f")
494	        if isinstance(value, int):
495	            return str(value)
496	        if isinstance(value, str):
497	            return _json_string(value)
498	        if isinstance(value, list):
499	            return "[" + ",".join(encode(v) for v in value) + "]"
500	        if isinstance(value, dict):
501	            return (
502	                "{"
503	                + ",".join(
504	                    f"{_json_string(k)}:{encode(v)}" for k, v in value.items()
505	                )
506	                + "}"
507	            )
508	        raise TypeError(f"cannot serialize {type(value).__name__}")
509	
510	    return encode(obj)
511	
512	
513	def _json_string(text: str) -> str:
514	    out = ['"']
515	    for ch in text:
516	        if ch == '"':
517	            out.append('\\"')
518	        elif ch == "\\":
519	            out.append("\\\\")
520	        elif ch == "\n":
521	            out.append("\\n")
522	        elif ch == "\r":
523	            out.append("\\r")
524	        elif ch == "\t":
525	            out.append("\\t")
526	        elif ord(ch) < 0x20:
527	            out.append(f"\\u{ord(ch):04x}")
528	        else:
529	            out.append(ch)
530	    out.append('"')
531	    return "".join(out)
532	
533	
534	def execute(data_dir: str, sql: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
535	    """Run *sql* against CSV tables in *data_dir*; return a result dict.
536	
537	    Raises:
538	        FileNotFoundError: the table's CSV file does not exist.
539	        KeyError: the query references a column absent from the header.
540	        ValueError: the SQL is malformed/unsupported, or a required field
541	            cannot be read as a decimal number.
542	    """
543	    query: Query = parse_sql(sql)
544	    table_path = Path(data_dir) / f"{query.table}.csv"
545	    # Built-in open raises FileNotFoundError, preserving the required type.
546	    with open(table_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
547	        reader = csv.reader(fh)
548	        try:
549	            header = next(reader)
550	        except StopIteration:
551	            header = []
552	        for name in query.required_columns():
553	            if name not in header:
554	                raise KeyError(
555	                    f"column {name!r} does not exist in table {query.table!r}"
556	                )
557	        result = _run_batches(reader, query, header)
558	        # ORDER BY sorts the fully computed result rows; LIMIT truncates last.
559	        if query.order_by:

"""Baseline tests for the OLAP Turbo query engine."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
import sys
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from olap_turbo import execute
from olap_turbo.engine import BATCH_SIZE, render
from olap_turbo.sql import parse_sql

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


@pytest.fixture()
def data_dir(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    (tmp_path / "sales.csv").write_text(
        "id,region,amount,note\n"
        "1,east,10,a\n"
        "2,west,20.5,b\n"
        "3,east,30,\n"
        "4,east,abc,x\n"
        "5,west,-2.25,y\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    return tmp_path


# ---------- projection queries ----------

def test_projection_order_and_filter(data_dir):
    result = execute(str(data_dir), 'SELECT amount, id FROM sales WHERE region = "east"')
    assert result["columns"] == ["amount", "id"]
    assert result["rows"] == [[10, 1], [30, 3], ["abc", 4]]
    assert result["row_count"] == 3


def test_projection_preserves_csv_order(data_dir):
    result = execute(str(data_dir), "SELECT id FROM sales WHERE id >= 2")
    assert [r[0] for r in result["rows"]] == [2, 3, 4, 5]


def test_all_operators_numeric(data_dir):
    assert execute(str(data_dir), "SELECT id FROM sales WHERE id > 2")["rows"] == [[3], [4], [5]]
    assert execute(str(data_dir), "SELECT id FROM sales WHERE id >= 2")["rows"] == [[2], [3], [4], [5]]
    assert execute(str(data_dir), "SELECT id FROM sales WHERE id < 3")["rows"] == [[1], [2]]
    assert execute(str(data_dir), "SELECT id FROM sales WHERE id <= 2")["rows"] == [[1], [2]]
    assert execute(str(data_dir), "SELECT id FROM sales WHERE id != 1")["rows"] == [[2], [3], [4], [5]]

        # composites span multiple batches.

    total_count = sum(c for c, _ in seen.values())
    assert total_count == n
    total_sum = sum(s for _, s in seen.values())

    assert (result["rows"][0][0], result["rows"][0][1]) == ("a", "C")


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql",
    [
        # SELECT must list every GROUP BY column, in the same order
        "SELECT a, count(*), sum(x) FROM t GROUP BY a, b",
        "SELECT b, a, count(*), sum(x) FROM t GROUP BY a, b",
        "SELECT a, b, count(*), sum(x) FROM t GROUP BY b, a",
        # GROUP BY columns must be distinct, both in GROUP BY and SELECT
        "SELECT a, b, count(*), sum(x) FROM t GROUP BY a, a",
        "SELECT a, a, count(*), sum(x) FROM t GROUP BY a, a",
        # count(*) must follow the grouping columns
        "SELECT a, b, sum(x), count(*) FROM t GROUP BY a, b",
        "SELECT count(*), a, b, sum(x) FROM t GROUP BY a, b",
        # at least one aggregate, and only non-grouping aggregates
        "SELECT a, b, count(*) FROM t GROUP BY a, b",
        "SELECT a, b, count(*), median(x) FROM t GROUP BY a, b",
        "SELECT a, b, count(*), x, sum(y) FROM t GROUP BY a, b",
        "SELECT a, b, count(*), sum(a) FROM t GROUP BY a, b",
        "SELECT a, b, count(*), sum(b) FROM t GROUP BY a, b",
        "SELECT a, b, count(*), sum(x), sum(x) FROM t GROUP BY a, b",
        "SELECT a, b, count(*) FROM t GROUP BY a, b, c",
        # three-column GROUP BY follows the same rules
        "SELECT a, b, c, count(*), sum(a) FROM t GROUP BY a, b, c",
        "SELECT a, b, count(*), sum(x) FROM t GROUP BY a, b, c",
    ],
)
def test_bad_multi_grouped_sql_raises_valueerror(tmp_path, sql):
    (tmp_path / "t.csv").write_text(
        "a,b,c,x,y\n1,2,3,4,5\n", encoding="utf-8"

    [

def test_parse_sql_boolean_tree_shape():
    from olap_turbo.sql import BoolOp, Comparison

    q = parse_sql("SELECT a FROM t WHERE a = 1 OR b = 2 AND c = 3")
    assert isinstance(q.where, BoolOp)
    assert q.where.op == "OR"
    assert len(q.where.operands) == 2
    assert isinstance(q.where.operands[0], Comparison)
    right = q.where.operands[1]
    assert isinstance(right, BoolOp) and right.op == "AND"
    assert [c.column for c in right.operands] == ["b", "c"]
    # Parentheses do not add wrapper nodes around a single grouped expr.
    q2 = parse_sql("SELECT a FROM t WHERE (a = 1 OR b = 2) AND c = 3")
    assert q2.where.op == "AND"
    assert isinstance(q2.where.operands[0], BoolOp)
    assert q2.where.operands[0].op == "OR"
    # No WHERE stays None.
    assert parse_sql("SELECT a FROM t").where is None
    # Predicate columns are all required, in first-appearance order.
    assert q2.required_columns() == ("a", "b", "c")

def test_parse_sql_having_tree_shape():

    q = parse_sql(
        "SELECT count(*), sum(a) FROM t HAVING count(*) > 1 AND sum(a) <= 2 OR count(*) = 0"
    )

# ---------- HAVING error forms ----------

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql",
    [
        # HAVING on a plain projection query
        "SELECT a FROM t HAVING count(*) > 1",
        "SELECT a FROM t WHERE a = 1 HAVING count(*) > 1",
        # wrong position: before WHERE / before GROUP BY / between GROUP and BY
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING count(*) > 1 WHERE a = 1",
        "SELECT a, count(*), sum(b) FROM t HAVING count(*) > 1 GROUP BY a",
        "SELECT a, count(*), sum(b) FROM t GROUP HAVING count(*) > 1 BY a",
        # repeated HAVING
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING count(*) > 1 HAVING count(*) > 2",
        # left side must be a selected aggregate
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING sum(a) > 1",            # sum not selected
        "SELECT count(*), sum(a) FROM t HAVING sum(b) > 1",    # other sum
        "SELECT a, count(*), sum(b) FROM t GROUP BY a HAVING a > 1",      # grouping column
        "SELECT a, count(*), sum(b) FROM t GROUP BY a HAVING b > 1",      # plain column
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING 1 > count(*)",          # reversed sides
        # right side must be an unquoted finite decimal number
        'SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING count(*) > "1"',        # quoted value
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING count(*) > a",          # column value
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING count(*) > count(*)",   # aggregate value
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING count(*) > -",          # incomplete number
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING count(*) > 1.2.3",      # malformed number
        # NOT, other functions and other expression forms
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING NOT count(*) > 1",
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING avg(x) > 1",
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING count(col) > 1",
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING count(*) > 1 + 1",
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING count(*) ",             # incomplete condition
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING",                       # no condition
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING ()",                    # empty group
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING (count(*) > 1)",        # parens around one
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING ((count(*) > 1))",      # nested single
        # malformed operators / connectives / parens
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING count(*) >> 1",         # bad operator
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING count(*) >",            # missing value
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING count(*) > 1 AND",      # dangling AND
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING OR count(*) > 1",       # leading OR
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING count(*) > 1 OR",       # trailing OR
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING count(*) > 1 AND OR count(*) > 2",
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING (count(*) > 1",         # unmatched '('
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING count(*) > 1)",         # unmatched ')'
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t HAVING count(*) > 1 count(*) > 2",
        # same rules on grouped queries
        "SELECT a, count(*) FROM t GROUP BY a HAVING sum(a) > 1",
        "SELECT a, count(*), sum(b) FROM t GROUP BY a HAVING a = 1",
        'SELECT a, count(*), sum(b) FROM t GROUP BY a HAVING count(*) > "1"',
    ],
)

# ---------- ORDER BY / LIMIT error forms ----------

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql",
    [
        # sort items must reference result columns
        "SELECT a FROM t ORDER BY b",                      # unselected column
        "SELECT a FROM t ORDER BY count(*)",               # aggregate on projection
        "SELECT a FROM t ORDER BY sum(a)",                 # aggregate on projection
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t ORDER BY a",               # plain column on aggregate
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t ORDER BY sum(a)",          # unselected sum
        "SELECT count(*), sum(a) FROM t ORDER BY sum(b)",  # other sum
        "SELECT a, count(*), sum(b) FROM t GROUP BY a ORDER BY b",   # unselected column
        # duplicate sort items
        "SELECT a, b FROM t ORDER BY a, a",
        "SELECT a FROM t ORDER BY a ASC, a DESC",
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t ORDER BY count(*), count(*)",
        "SELECT count(*), sum(a) FROM t ORDER BY sum(a), sum(a)",
        # malformed sort items
        "SELECT a FROM t ORDER BY",          # missing item
        "SELECT a FROM t ORDER BY 1",        # number
        "SELECT a FROM t ORDER BY *",        # star
        "SELECT a FROM t ORDER BY avg(a)",   # unsupported function
        "SELECT a FROM t ORDER BY count(a)", # unsupported function
        "SELECT a FROM t ORDER BY (a)",      # parenthesized
        "SELECT a FROM t ORDER BY a b",      # missing comma
        "SELECT a FROM t ORDER a",           # missing BY
        "SELECT a FROM t BY a",              # BY without ORDER
        # clause order and repetition
        "SELECT a FROM t LIMIT 1 ORDER BY a",
        "SELECT a FROM t ORDER BY a ORDER BY a",
        "SELECT a FROM t LIMIT 1 LIMIT 2",
        "SELECT a FROM t ORDER BY a WHERE a = 1",
        "SELECT a FROM t ORDER BY a GROUP BY a",
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t ORDER BY count(*) HAVING count(*) > 1",
        "SELECT count(*) FROM t LIMIT 1 HAVING count(*) > 1",
        # LIMIT must be a non-negative decimal integer literal
        "SELECT a FROM t LIMIT",             # missing value
        "SELECT a FROM t LIMIT -1",          # negative
        "SELECT a FROM t LIMIT 1.5",         # fraction
        "SELECT a FROM t LIMIT 1.0",         # decimal point
        'SELECT a FROM t LIMIT "3"',         # string
        "SELECT a FROM t LIMIT a",           # column
        "SELECT a FROM t LIMIT 1+1",         # expression
        "SELECT a FROM t LIMIT 1 1",         # trailing token
    ],
)

        monkeypatch.setattr(engine_mod, "BATCH_SIZE", size)
        assert execute(str(tmp_path), sql) == expected


def test_parse_sql_avg_min_max_shape():
    from olap_turbo.sql import HavingComparison, SortItem

    q = parse_sql("SELECT count(*), avg(a), min(a), max(b) FROM t")
    assert [item.kind for item in q.select] == ["count_star", "avg", "min", "max"]
    assert q.select[1].text == "avg(a)"
    assert q.required_columns() == ("a", "b")
    q = parse_sql(
        "SELECT g, count(*), avg(v) FROM t GROUP BY g "
        "HAVING avg(v) > 1 ORDER BY avg(v) DESC LIMIT 3"
    )
    assert isinstance(q.having, HavingComparison)
    assert (q.having.kind, q.having.column, q.having.op) == ("avg", "v", ">")
    assert q.order_by == (SortItem("avg(v)", "avg", "v", True),)
    assert q.limit == 3


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql",
    [
        # each aggregate expression may appear only once
        "SELECT count(*), avg(a), avg(a) FROM t",
        "SELECT count(*), min(a), min(a) FROM t",
        "SELECT count(*), max(b), sum(b), max(b) FROM t",
        "SELECT a, count(*), avg(x), avg(x) FROM t GROUP BY a",
        "SELECT a, count(*), min(x), max(x), min(x) FROM t GROUP BY a",
        # grouping columns may not be aggregated
        "SELECT a, count(*), avg(a) FROM t GROUP BY a",
        "SELECT a, count(*), min(a) FROM t GROUP BY a",
        "SELECT a, count(*), max(a) FROM t GROUP BY a",
        # aggregates still require the aggregate query shape
        "SELECT avg(a) FROM t",
        "SELECT min(a), count(*) FROM t",
        "SELECT a, avg(b) FROM t",
        "SELECT a, count(*), max(b) FROM t",
        # unselected aggregates in HAVING / ORDER BY
        "SELECT count(*), avg(a) FROM t HAVING max(a) > 1",
        "SELECT a, count(*), avg(b) FROM t GROUP BY a HAVING min(b) > 1",
        "SELECT count(*), avg(a) FROM t ORDER BY min(a)",
        "SELECT count(*), avg(a) FROM t ORDER BY avg(a), avg(a)",
        # still-unsupported functions stay rejected everywhere
        "SELECT count(*), median(a) FROM t",
        "SELECT count(*), avg(a) FROM t HAVING median(a) > 1",
        "SELECT count(*), avg(a) FROM t ORDER BY median(a)",
    ],
)
def test_bad_avg_min_max_sql_raises_valueerror(tmp_path, sql):

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):

1	"""Minimal self-contained SQL lexer and parser.
2	
3	Supported grammar (the complete surface for this baseline)::
4	
5	    query      := SELECT select_list FROM identifier
6	                  [ WHERE boolean ] [ GROUP BY identifier (, identifier)* ]
7	                  [ HAVING having_boolean ]
8	                  [ ORDER BY sort_item (, sort_item)* ] [ LIMIT integer ]
9	    sort_item  := (identifier | count_star | agg_expr) [ ASC | DESC ]
10	    agg_expr   := sum_expr | avg_expr | min_expr | max_expr
11	    select_list:= grouping_column (, grouping_column)*,
12	                  count_star, agg_expr (, agg_expr)*   (grouped aggregate query)
13	                | count_star [, agg_expr ]*            (aggregate query)
14	                | column (, column)*                   (projection query)
15	    boolean    := or_expr
16	    or_expr    := and_expr (OR and_expr)*
17	    and_expr   := factor (AND factor)*
18	    factor     := LPAREN or_expr RPAREN | comparison
19	    comparison := identifier op value
20	    op         := = | != | > | >= | < | <=
21	    value      := number-literal | double-quoted-string-literal
22	
23	HAVING shares the AND/OR/parentheses boolean shape, but its leaves are
24	aggregate-to-number comparisons::
25	
26	    having_boolean := having_or
27	    having_factor  := LPAREN having_or RPAREN | having_comparison
28	    having_comparison := aggregate op number-literal
29	    aggregate      := count_star | agg_expr
30	
31	The left side must be a ``count(*)``, ``sum(column)``, ``avg(column)``,
32	``min(column)`` or ``max(column)`` expression that already appears in the
33	SELECT list; the right side is an unquoted finite decimal literal only (no
34	strings, no columns, no other expressions).
35	
36	AND binds tighter than OR; parentheses may be nested to override the
37	precedence. Parentheses *combine* boolean conditions only: a parenthesized
38	group must itself contain an AND/OR combination (``(a = 1)`` is rejected),
39	and parentheses may never wrap columns, values or comparisons-as-values.
40	There is no NOT, no constant truth value and no other expression forms.
41	
42	HAVING may appear at most once and only after GROUP BY (or after WHERE in
43	an ungrouped aggregate query); it is rejected on plain projection queries.
44	
45	ORDER BY follows HAVING (or WHERE/GROUP BY when HAVING is absent) and LIMIT
46	follows ORDER BY; each may appear at most once and never out of order. Each
47	sort item references a result column already in the SELECT list — a plain or
48	grouping column, ``count(*)`` or one of ``sum(column)``, ``avg(column)``,
49	``min(column)``, ``max(column)`` — with an optional ``ASC`` (default) or
50	``DESC`` direction; duplicate sort items and references to expressions
51	absent from the SELECT list are rejected. LIMIT takes a single non-negative
52	decimal integer literal (digits only: no sign, no fraction, no strings,
53	columns or expressions).
54	
55	A grouped query names one or more distinct grouping columns (at least two
56	for the multi-column shape): they must head the SELECT list in the same
57	order as the GROUP BY list, followed by count(*) and one or more distinct
58	aggregate expressions (``sum``/``avg``/``min``/``max`` over a column).
59	Every aggregate expression — the function name plus its column — may appear
60	at most once in a SELECT list, in grouped and ungrouped queries alike.
61	
62	Anything else (missing FROM, NOT, functions other than
63	count(*)/sum()/avg()/min()/max() in SELECT, wildcards, extra clauses,
64	malformed syntax, unmatched parentheses, OR outside WHERE/HAVING) raises
65	:class:`ValueError`.
66	"""
67	
68	from __future__ import annotations
69	
70	from dataclasses import dataclass
71	from enum import Enum
72	from typing import List, Optional, Tuple, Union

75	class _TokKind(Enum):
76	    IDENT = "ident"
77	    KEYWORD = "keyword"
78	    NUMBER = "number"
79	    STRING = "string"
80	    OP = "op"
81	    COMMA = "comma"
82	    STAR = "star"
83	    LPAREN = "lparen"
84	    RPAREN = "rparen"
85	    EOF = "eof"

87	
88	_KEYWORDS = {
89	    "SELECT", "FROM", "WHERE", "AND", "OR", "NOT", "GROUP", "BY", "HAVING",
90	    "ORDER", "LIMIT",
91	}

94	@dataclass
95	class _Token:
96	    kind: _TokKind
97	    text: str
98

100	def _tokenize(sql: str) -> List[_Token]:
101	    tokens: List[_Token] = []
102	    i, n = 0, len(sql)
103	    while i < n:
104	        c = sql[i]
105	        if c.isspace():
106	            i += 1
107	            continue
108	        if c == ",":
109	            tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.COMMA, c))
110	            i += 1
111	            continue
112	        if c == "(":
113	            tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.LPAREN, c))
114	            i += 1
115	            continue
116	        if c == ")":
117	            tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.RPAREN, c))
118	            i += 1
119	            continue
120	        if c == "*":
121	            tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.STAR, c))
122	            i += 1
123	            continue
124	        if c == '"':
125	            j = i + 1
126	            buf: List[str] = []
127	            while j < n and sql[j] != '"':
128	                buf.append(sql[j])
129	                j += 1
130	            if j >= n:
131	                raise ValueError("unterminated string literal in query")
132	            tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.STRING, "".join(buf)))
133	            i = j + 1
134	            continue
135	        if c in "=<>":
136	            if i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
137	                tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.OP, c + "="))
138	                i += 2
139	            else:
140	                tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.OP, c))
141	                i += 1
142	            continue
143	        if c == "!":
144	            if i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
145	                tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.OP, "!="))
146	                i += 2
147	                continue
148	            raise ValueError(f"unexpected character '!' at position {i}")
149	        if c.isdigit() or (c == "-" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1].isdigit()):
150	            j = i + 1
151	            while j < n and (sql[j].isdigit() or sql[j] == "."):
152	                j += 1
153	            text = sql[i:j]
154	            # Reject malformed numbers such as "1.2.3".
155	            _parse_decimal(text)
156	            tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.NUMBER, text))
157	            i = j
158	            continue
159	        if c.isalpha() or c == "_":
160	            j = i + 1
161	            while j < n and (sql[j].isalnum() or sql[j] == "_"):
162	                j += 1
163	            text = sql[i:j]
164	            upper = text.upper()
165	            kind = _TokKind.KEYWORD if upper in _KEYWORDS else _TokKind.IDENT
166	            tokens.append(_Token(kind, upper if kind is _TokKind.KEYWORD else text))
167	            i = j
168	            continue
169	        raise ValueError(f"unexpected character {c!r} at position {i}")
170	    tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.EOF, ""))
171	    return tokens

174	def _parse_decimal(text: str):
175	    """Validate a decimal numeric literal; return a Decimal-like float-free value."""
176	    from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation
177	
178	    try:
179	        return Decimal(text)
180	    except InvalidOperation:
181	        raise ValueError(f"invalid numeric literal {text!r}")

185	class Comparison:

198	    (:class:`Comparison` for WHERE, :class:`HavingComparison` for HAVING)
199	    or further :class:`BoolOp` nodes.

214	    ``"max"`` (with ``column`` naming the aggregated column); ``text`` is
215	    the aggregate's SELECT expression text.
216	    """

219	    kind: str

221	    value_text: str

229	
230	@dataclass(frozen=True)

232	    # Original expression text as written in the query, e.g. "count(*)",
233	    # "sum(a)", "avg(a)".

235	    kind: str  # "column" | "count_star" | "sum" | "avg" | "min" | "max"

253	@dataclass(frozen=True)

259	    having: Optional[HavingExpr] = None
260	    order_by: Tuple[SortItem, ...] = ()

263	    @property
264	    def is_aggregate(self) -> bool:

271	    def required_columns(self) -> Tuple[str, ...]:
272	        """Columns the scan must materialize (group key, aggregates, predicates)."""
273	        cols: List[str] = []
274	        seen = set()
275	        for item in self.select:
276	            if item.kind == "column":
277	                if item.column not in seen:
278	                    seen.add(item.column)
279	                    cols.append(item.column)
280	            elif item.kind in _AGG_KINDS and item.column not in seen:

288	    def _collect_where_columns(
289	        node: WhereExpr, cols: List[str], seen: set
290	    ) -> None:

292	            if node.column not in seen:
293	                seen.add(node.column)
294	                cols.append(node.column)

296	        for operand in node.operands:
297	            Query._collect_where_columns(operand, cols, seen)

300	_OPS = {"=", "!=", ">", ">=", "<", "<="}

306	class _Parser:
307	    def __init__(self, sql: str):

311	    def _peek(self) -> _Token:
312	        return self.tokens[self.pos]
313	
314	    def _next(self) -> _Token:
315	        tok = self.tokens[self.pos]
316	        self.pos += 1
317	        return tok
318	
319	    def _expect_keyword(self, word: str) -> None:
320	        tok = self._next()

322	            raise ValueError(f"expected {word} but found {tok.text!r}")
323	
324	    def _accept_keyword(self, word: str) -> bool:
325	        tok = self._peek()
326	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.KEYWORD and tok.text == word:
327	            self._next()
328	            return True
329	        return False
330	
331	    def parse(self) -> Query:
332	        self._expect_keyword("SELECT")
333	        items = self._parse_select_list()
334	        self._expect_keyword("FROM")
335	        table_tok = self._next()
336	        if table_tok.kind is not _TokKind.IDENT:
337	            raise ValueError("table name must be a simple identifier")
338	        where: Optional[WhereExpr] = None
339	        having: Optional[HavingExpr] = None
340	        group_by: List[str] = []
341	        order_by: List[SortItem] = []
342	        limit: Optional[int] = None
343	        tok = self._peek()
344	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.KEYWORD and tok.text == "WHERE":

346	            where = self._parse_or()
347	            tok = self._peek()

393	            table_tok.text,

396	            having,

401	    def _validate_grouped(
402	        self, items: List[SelectItem], group_by: List[str]
403	    ) -> None:
404	        """Enforce the grouped shape.
405	
406	        SELECT leads with the GROUP BY columns in the same order (distinct),
407	        followed by count(*) and one or more distinct aggregate expressions
408	        (sum/avg/min/max over a non-grouping column).
409	        """
410	        if len(group_by) != len(set(group_by)):
411	            raise ValueError("GROUP BY may not list the same column twice")
412	        if len(items) < len(group_by) + 2:
413	            raise ValueError(
414	                "grouped SELECT must list the grouping columns followed by "
415	                "count(*) and one or more aggregate expressions"
416	            )
417	        for pos, group_col in enumerate(group_by):
418	            item = items[pos]
419	            if item.kind != "column" or item.column != group_col:
420	                raise ValueError(
421	                    "SELECT grouping columns must lead the SELECT list in "
422	                    "the same order as GROUP BY"
423	                )
424	        if items[len(group_by)].kind != "count_star":
425	            raise ValueError(
426	                "grouped SELECT must list count(*) after the grouping columns"
427	            )
428	        seen_aggs = set()
429	        for item in items[len(group_by) + 1 :]:
430	            if item.kind not in _AGG_KINDS:
431	                raise ValueError(
432	                    "grouped SELECT may only contain the grouping columns, "
433	                    "count(*) and sum/avg/min/max aggregates"
434	                )
435	            key = (item.kind, item.column)
436	            if key in seen_aggs:
437	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate aggregate {item.text}")
438	            if item.column in group_by:

441	                )

444	    def _parse_select_list(self) -> List[SelectItem]:
445	        items = [self._parse_select_item()]
446	        while self._peek().kind is _TokKind.COMMA:
447	            self._next()
448	            items.append(self._parse_select_item())
449	        return items
450	
451	    def _validate_ungrouped(self, items: List[SelectItem]) -> None:
452	        """Rules for queries without GROUP BY (the baseline shapes)."""
453	        if items[0].kind in _AGG_KINDS:
454	            raise ValueError(
455	                f"{items[0].kind}(column) requires count(*) in the SELECT list"
456	            )
457	        aggregate = items[0].kind == "count_star"
458	        seen_aggs = set()
459	        for item in items[1:]:
460	            if aggregate:
461	                if item.kind not in _AGG_KINDS:
462	                    raise ValueError(
463	                        "aggregate SELECT may only contain count(*) and "
464	                        "sum/avg/min/max aggregates"
465	                    )
466	                key = (item.kind, item.column)
467	                if key in seen_aggs:
468	                    raise ValueError(f"duplicate aggregate {item.text}")
469	                seen_aggs.add(key)
470	            elif item.kind in _AGG_KINDS:
471	                raise ValueError(
472	                    f"{item.kind}(column) requires count(*) in the SELECT list"
473	                )
474	            elif item.kind != "column":
475	                raise ValueError(
476	                    "count(*)/aggregates cannot be mixed with plain columns"
477	                )
478	
479	    def _parse_select_item(self) -> SelectItem:
480	        tok = self._peek()
481	        # function form: ident '(' ... ')'
482	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.IDENT and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind is _TokKind.LPAREN:
483	            name_tok = self._next()
484	            self._next()  # (
485	            inner = self._next()
486	            self._expect(_TokKind.RPAREN)
487	            upper = name_tok.text.upper()
488	            if upper == "COUNT" and inner.kind is _TokKind.STAR:
489	                return SelectItem("count(*)", "count_star")
490	            if upper in ("SUM", "AVG", "MIN", "MAX") and inner.kind is _TokKind.IDENT:
491	                kind = upper.lower()
492	                return SelectItem(f"{kind}({inner.text})", kind, inner.text)
493	            # Any other function (count(col), median, ...) is unsupported.
494	            raise ValueError(
495	                f"unsupported SELECT expression {name_tok.text}({inner.text})"
496	            )
497	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.STAR:
498	            raise ValueError("wildcard column '*' is not supported")
499	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.IDENT:
500	            self._next()
501	            return SelectItem(tok.text, "column", tok.text)
502	        raise ValueError(f"invalid SELECT item {tok.text!r}")
503	
504	    def _expect(self, kind: _TokKind) -> _Token:
505	        tok = self._next()
506	        if tok.kind is not kind:
507	            raise ValueError(f"expected {kind.value} but found {tok.text!r}")
508	        return tok
509	
510	    # ----- WHERE boolean grammar: or_expr := and_expr (OR and_expr)* -----
511	
512	    def _parse_or(self) -> WhereExpr:
513	        operands = [self._parse_and()]
514	        while self._accept_keyword("OR"):
515	            operands.append(self._parse_and())
516	        if len(operands) == 1:
517	            return operands[0]
518	        return BoolOp("OR", tuple(operands))
519	
520	    def _parse_and(self) -> WhereExpr:
521	        operands = [self._parse_factor()]
522	        while self._accept_keyword("AND"):

524	        if len(operands) == 1:

527	
528	    def _parse_factor(self) -> WhereExpr:
529	        tok = self._peek()

531	            self._next()
532	            node = self._parse_or()
533	            self._expect(_TokKind.RPAREN)
534	            if isinstance(node, Comparison):

536	                # not wrap a single comparison, a column or a value.

539	                    "not a single comparison"
540	                )

542	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.IDENT:

545	        # boolean condition.

548	    def _parse_comparison(self) -> Comparison:
549	        col = self._expect(_TokKind.IDENT)

559	            "comparison value must be an unquoted number or a double-quoted string"
560	        )
561	
562	    # ----- HAVING boolean grammar: aggregate op number, AND/OR/parens -----
563	
564	    def _parse_having_or(self) -> HavingExpr:
565	        operands = [self._parse_having_and()]
566	        while self._accept_keyword("OR"):
567	            operands.append(self._parse_having_and())
568	        if len(operands) == 1:
569	            return operands[0]

571	
572	    def _parse_having_and(self) -> HavingExpr:
573	        operands = [self._parse_having_factor()]
574	        while self._accept_keyword("AND"):
575	            operands.append(self._parse_having_factor())
576	        if len(operands) == 1:
577	            return operands[0]

579	
580	    def _parse_having_factor(self) -> HavingExpr:
581	        tok = self._peek()
582	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.LPAREN:
583	            self._next()
584	            node = self._parse_having_or()
585	            self._expect(_TokKind.RPAREN)
586	            if isinstance(node, HavingComparison):
587	                # As in WHERE, parentheses only combine conditions; they
588	                # may not wrap a single HAVING comparison.
589	                raise ValueError(
590	                    "parentheses may only group combined AND/OR conditions, "
591	                    "not a single comparison"
592	                )

594	        if (
595	            tok.kind is _TokKind.IDENT
596	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind is _TokKind.LPAREN
597	        ):
598	            return self._parse_having_comparison()
599	        # Plain columns/grouping columns, NOT, numbers, dangling AND/OR,
600	        # ')', EOF, ...: none can start a HAVING aggregate comparison.
601	        raise ValueError(
602	            "HAVING condition must compare count(*) or a "
603	            "sum/avg/min/max aggregate with a number, but found "
604	            f"{tok.text!r}"
605	        )
606	
607	    def _parse_having_comparison(self) -> HavingComparison:
608	        name_tok = self._next()  # the aggregate identifier
609	        self._next()  # LPAREN
610	        inner = self._next()
611	        self._expect(_TokKind.RPAREN)
612	        upper = name_tok.text.upper()
613	        if upper == "COUNT" and inner.kind is _TokKind.STAR:
614	            text, kind, column = "count(*)", "count_star", None
615	        elif upper in ("SUM", "AVG", "MIN", "MAX") and inner.kind is _TokKind.IDENT:
616	            kind = upper.lower()
617	            text, column = f"{kind}({inner.text})", inner.text
618	        else:
619	            raise ValueError(
620	                "HAVING may only compare count(*) or sum/avg/min/max "
621	                "aggregates"
622	            )
623	        op_tok = self._expect(_TokKind.OP)
624	        if op_tok.text not in _OPS:
625	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported operator {op_tok.text!r}")
626	        val = self._next()
627	        if val.kind is not _TokKind.NUMBER:
628	            # Quoted strings, columns, aggregates, keywords, EOF: HAVING
629	            # compares aggregates against finite decimal literals only.
630	            raise ValueError(
631	                "HAVING comparison value must be an unquoted finite decimal number"
632	            )
633	        return HavingComparison(text, kind, op_tok.text, val.text, column)
634	
635	    def _validate_having_aggregates(
636	        self, node: HavingExpr, items: List[SelectItem]
637	    ) -> None:
638	        """Every HAVING aggregate must already appear in the SELECT list."""
639	        if isinstance(node, BoolOp):
640	            for operand in node.operands:
641	                self._validate_having_aggregates(operand, items)

643	        for item in items:
644	            if item.kind == node.kind and item.column == node.column:
645	                return

647	            f"HAVING aggregate {node.text} is not in the SELECT list"
648	        )
649	
650	    # ----- ORDER BY / LIMIT -----
651	
652	    def _parse_sort_item(self, items: List[SelectItem]) -> SortItem:
653	        tok = self._peek()
654	        if (
655	            tok.kind is _TokKind.IDENT
656	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind is _TokKind.LPAREN
657	        ):
658	            name_tok = self._next()
659	            self._next()  # (
660	            inner = self._next()
661	            self._expect(_TokKind.RPAREN)
662	            upper = name_tok.text.upper()
663	            if upper == "COUNT" and inner.kind is _TokKind.STAR:

677	            # Numbers, strings, keywords, '*', parens, EOF: none can start
678	            # a sort item.
679	            raise ValueError(f"invalid ORDER BY item {tok.text!r}")

681	        # named e.g. "asc" remains usable elsewhere in the grammar.
682	        descending = False

684	        if nxt.kind is _TokKind.IDENT and nxt.text.upper() in ("ASC", "DESC"):

688	        self._validate_sort_item(sort_item, items)

692	        self, sort_item: SortItem, items: List[SelectItem]
693	    ) -> None:
694	        """Every ORDER BY item must reference a column of the result."""
695	        for item in items:
696	            if item.kind == sort_item.kind and item.column == sort_item.column:

701	            )
